title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in Grothendieck's notes on the divided-power de Rham complex, c_{i,j} = (i+j)!/(i! j!) is the binomial coefficient giving the multiplication of divided powers: x^{[i]} x^{[j]} = c_{i,j} x^{[i+j]}. Lemma 2 (stated on the previous page) says: for i, j ≥ 0 there is an l ≥ 0 such that c_{i+j,l} and c_{i,j+l} are both nonzero mod p.

On the previous page he proved this by an explicit digit-by-digit addition with carries. He takes l with p-adic digits l_α = p-1-σ_α, where σ_α are the digits of i+j. That makes i+j+l = p^{r+2} - 1.

On this page he crosses that out and gives a shorter proof:
- Choose r with p^r > i+j and set l = p^r - 1 - (i+j), which is ≥ 0.
- Then i+j+l = p^r - 1 = Σ_{α=0}^{r-1} (p-1) p^α, so every base-p digit equals p-1.
- The sum can be bracketed as (i+j)+l or as i+(j+l). Either way, adding the two summands in base p involves no carries, since each digit pair must add to exactly p-1.
- By the usual criterion (Kummer/Lucas), both c_{i+j,l} and c_{i,j+l} are prime to p.

In a closing NB he isolates the common lemma behind Lemmas 1 and 2: if μ + ν = p^r - 1, then c_{μ,ν} is nonzero mod p. A sharper statement, 'plus précisément c_{μ,ν} ...', was begun and struck out; the natural completion is c_{μ,ν} ≡ (-1)^ν mod p.

Purpose: such nonvanishing statements in the divided-power algebra Γ_{F_p}[x] (or the dual algebra) let one move any x^{[i]} x^{[j]}-type product to the top-type element x^{[p^r-1]} with a unit coefficient. This is presumably used for a nondegeneracy, non-zero-divisor or generation statement in the PD de Rham complex in characteristic p. The next page goes on to p-adic valuations of factorials via Legendre's formula.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument is correct and complete: p^r > i+j ensures l ≥ 0, and the no-carry condition follows because every digit of p^r - 1 is p-1.
Minor point: the previous page's construction gives an l with i+j+l = p^{r+2} - 1; this page's version simply takes the minimal power. It is the same idea, streamlined.

ideas.what: Choose l = p^r - 1 - (i+j) so that both bracketings (i+j)+l and i+(j+l) are carry-free; deduce that both binomial coefficients are prime to p
ideas.modern_name: Kummer's theorem / Lucas's theorem on binomial coefficients mod p

ideas.what: For μ+ν = p^r - 1, the coefficient binom(μ+ν, μ) is nonzero mod p (indeed it is ≡ (-1)^ν)
ideas.modern_name: standard consequence of Lucas's theorem; relevant to the structure of divided-power algebras in characteristic p

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary combinatorial lemma on binomial coefficients mod p (Kummer/Lucas), used as a technical step in divided-power computations. It is correct, standard and routine.
transcription_corrections: 'on [?] {+sait [?]+} que l'on a' is better read as 'on voit que l'on a' (after the struck 'je dis que').
The line '(i+j)+l = i+(j+l)' is a marginal insertion written just above 'On sait alors, par le critère habituel'.
The struck final line reads '(plus précisément, c_{μ,ν} ...' with something like 'c_{μ,ν} ≡ ...' crossed out.
